messages:
maria: Quick heads-up - last hour we saw a 3x spike in requests pinned to v1 for tenant-73 during the ETL window. Some latency degradations and queueing.
jon: Is that the same tenant that hit the quota throttle yesterday? :confused:
sam: yep same. Their traffic pattern is bursty (batching). Our current v1->v2 soft-fallback only triggers on capacity errors, not surge patterns.
maria: Proposal: add a SurgeProtection routing policy that temporarily routes a configurable percent of traffic to v2 when short-term qps exceeds X percentile for a tenant. Keep it conservative (10-25%) and only for <5m windows.
olivia: I like the idea. Two questions: how do we signal this in the console (so customers aren't surprised), and how do we measure false positives? We don't want silent behavior changes.
jon: For the console UX: show a toast on the tenant details with "Automatic surge mitigation active - routing 20% of traffic to v2 for 3m" and a link to opt-out for that tenant. Also surface it in the routing timeline.
sam: Telemetry-wise we should sample pre- and post-routing pairs and compute per-token latency/delta and token-quality score (we have eval sets for most customers). Metric names: surge.probe.latency, surge.probe.quality.
maria: Implementation sketch (runtime):
```
routing.policy.surge.enabled = true
routing.policy.surge.window = 60s
routing.policy.surge.threshold_p99 = 1.4  # 140% of baseline
routing.policy.surge.shift_pct = 0.2
routing.policy.surge.cooldown = 300s
```
jon: Note: baseline needs smoothing per-tenant. Use EWMA on qps with a 10m half-life, avoid daily cron spikes.
olivia: Console copy: "During short bursts, Redwood may route a small portion of your traffic to a compatible model variant to preserve latency for the rest of your requests. This is automatic and reversible; opt-out available." Keep legal/marketing in the loop.
sam: Also need to account for quota accounting. If we route to v2 which has different token pricing, billing team wants visibility. Suggest we tag routed requests with header `X-Routed-By: surge-protect/1` and add a billing flag to separate costing.
maria: Good call. Also add a telemetry tag so we can rollback the policy quickly: `surge_experiment_id` in traces.
jon: How do we avoid oscillation? If tenant spikes, routes some to v2, then they throttle, then drop, then re-trigger. Need hysteresis. Use cooldown plus require two consecutive windows above threshold before engaging.
olivia: UX: show recent surge events on tenant timeline (last 24h) and an aggregate "surge mitigations applied" counter. We should also provide a webhook alert (customer-specified) when surge mitigation runs more than N times in 24h.
sam: We should test by shadowing first. Plan: implement sampling routing (no actual redirect) for 48h for a small set of tenants, then opt-in canary to 10 tenants, then gradual 1% rollout.
maria: For safe defaults: window=60s, threshold=1.5, shift_pct=0.15, cooldown=300s, min_qps=20. Keep off for tenants with eval mismatches.
jon: Ops runbook snippet: if surge protection causes quality regressions, toggle `routing.policy.surge.enabled=false` and mark tenant exempt with `surge.exempt=true` in console.
deploy-bot: deploy: routing-service v2.14 -> prod in 5m :rocket:
maria: Thanks - I'll draft the RFC + console mocks and ping billing/legal. I'll add telemetry dashboard tiles: (1) surge.events.count, (2) surge.probe.latency.delta_p50/p95, (3) surge.routed.token_count. Ping me for review.
olivia: +1. Also file a short SOC note for enterprise customers explaining opt-out and billing effects.
jon: I'll own the smoke tests: simulate bursts using loadgen and assert no more than 10% p99 increase across unaffected requests.
maria: Cool. Let's regroup after the canary. :thumbsup:
